events.title: The Orient Express makes its first run
events.description: The first Orient Express left Paris on its inaugural journey toward Constantinople. It was operated by the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits and linked Western Europe with the edge of Asia in comfort.
events.significance: The train became a symbol of luxury travel and international intrigue. It helped shape the idea of glamorous long-distance rail journeys.

events.title: Marshall proposes European recovery aid
events.description: In a commencement address at Harvard University, U.S. Secretary of State George C. Marshall outlined a plan for American economic assistance to rebuild war-torn Europe.
events.significance: The Marshall Plan helped revive Western European economies and strengthen democratic alliances. It also became a cornerstone of early Cold War policy.

events.title: The Six-Day War begins
events.description: Israel launched preemptive air strikes against Egypt, followed by ground operations against Egypt, Jordan and Syria, opening a brief but decisive war.
events.significance: Israel's gains in the war redrew the map of the Middle East. The territorial questions that followed remain central to the region's politics today.

events.title: Robert F. Kennedy is shot in Los Angeles
events.description: Moments after winning the California Democratic presidential primary, Senator Robert F. Kennedy was shot at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles. He died the following day.
events.significance: The assassination, coming only weeks after Martin Luther King Jr.'s death, deepened the sense of national turmoil in 1968. It also changed the course of that year's presidential race.

events.title: First cases of what became known as AIDS are reported
events.description: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported a rare pneumonia in five previously healthy gay men in Los Angeles.
events.significance: This report is widely regarded as the first public notice of the AIDS epidemic. It launched decades of research and public health response.
